story.story:
Little Red Riding Hood’s mother tucked bread and a small cake into a wicker basket. “Take these to Grandmother’s cottage, and stay on the forest path.” Red tied her scarlet hood and set off.

Under an oak tree, a wolf stepped onto the path. “Where are you going?” he asked.

“To Grandmother’s cottage beside the three birch trees,” Red replied.

“Why not bring her flowers?” suggested the wolf. While Red picked daisies, he raced ahead.

At the cottage’s green front door, the wolf knocked and called in a sweet voice, “It’s Little Red Riding Hood!”

“Lift the latch,” Grandmother answered from bed.

The wolf rushed inside and swallowed her whole. He put on her nightcap, pulled her quilt over himself, and waited.

Red arrived, pushed open the green door, and placed her basket on the wooden table. She approached the bed.

“Grandmother, what big ears you have!”

“All the better to hear you with.”

“What big eyes you have!”

“All the better to see you with.”

Red gripped her cloak. “What big teeth you have!”

“All the better to eat you with!”

The wolf sprang up. Red screamed, but he swallowed her whole. Then he fell asleep, snoring loudly.

A passing woodcutter heard the snores and entered through the green door. Seeing the wolf’s swollen belly, he carefully snipped it open. Red scrambled out, then helped Grandmother climb free. Trembling with relief, they hugged.

They filled the sleeping wolf’s belly with stones. When he awoke, he stumbled and fell dead.

Grandmother shared the cake with her rescuers. Red promised never to wander from the path again.

blocking.title: Little Red Riding Hood
blocking.style: Watercolor and colored-pencil storybook illustrations; woodland greens, warm cream, and a scarlet cloak; soft morning sunlight outdoors, cool shadows inside the cottage, and warm light after the rescue.
blocking.story:
Little Red Riding Hood’s mother tucked bread and a small cake into a wicker basket. “Take these to Grandmother’s cottage, where she keeps her quilt and nightcap on her bed and a needle and thread in her bedside sewing basket, and stay on the forest path, where daisies grow along the edges.” Red tied her scarlet hood and set off.

Under an oak tree, a wolf stepped onto the path. “Where are you going?” he asked.

“To Grandmother’s cottage beside the three birch trees,” Red replied.

“Why not bring her flowers?” suggested the wolf. While Red picked daisies, he raced ahead.

At the cottage’s green front door, the wolf knocked and called in a sweet voice, “It’s Little Red Riding Hood!”

“Lift the latch,” Grandmother answered from bed.

The wolf rushed inside and swallowed her whole. He put on her nightcap, pulled her quilt over himself, and waited.

Red arrived, pushed open the green door, and placed her basket on the wooden table. She approached the bed.

“Grandmother, what big ears you have!”

“All the better to hear you with.”

“What big eyes you have!”

“All the better to see you with.”

Red gripped her cloak. “What big teeth you have!”

“All the better to eat you with!”

The wolf sprang up. Red screamed, but he swallowed her whole. Then he fell asleep, snoring loudly.

A passing woodcutter heard the snores and entered through the green door. Seeing the wolf’s swollen belly, he took a pair of shears from his belt and carefully snipped it open. Red scrambled out, then helped Grandmother climb free. Trembling with relief, they hugged.

They filled the sleeping wolf’s belly with stones gathered from outside the cottage. Grandmother stitched the wolf’s belly shut with a needle and thread from her bedside sewing basket. When he awoke, he stumbled and fell dead.

Grandmother shared the cake with her rescuers. Red promised never to wander from the path again.

asset_specs.name: Little Red Riding Hood
asset_specs.height: A small child, about three-fifths the height of a grown person.
asset_specs.spec: A small, slender girl with warm light skin, a round face, rosy cheeks, and brown eyes. Her chestnut-brown hair forms two short braids reaching her shoulders, each tied with a cream ribbon. She wears a scarlet, knee-length hooded cloak tied beneath her chin, with a roomy hood covering the crown of her head. Beneath it are a long-sleeved warm-cream dress, a moss-green apron, cream stockings, and plain brown leather shoes.

asset_specs.name: Little Red Riding Hood’s mother
asset_specs.spec: A grown woman of average build with warm light skin, a softly rounded face, and brown eyes. Her chestnut-brown hair is parted in the middle and gathered into a low bun. She wears an ankle-length sage-green dress with long sleeves, a warm-cream apron tied at the waist, and plain brown leather shoes.

asset_specs.name: bread
asset_specs.height: A small loaf about 22 cm long, comfortably held in two adult hands.
asset_specs.spec: A single oval loaf with a domed top, a flat underside, and a golden-brown crust. Three diagonal scoring marks cross the top, exposing paler cream-colored ridges of baked dough.

asset_specs.name: small cake
asset_specs.height: A small cake about 12 cm across and 5 cm high, fitting on one outstretched adult hand.
asset_specs.spec: A low, round cake with golden sides and a flat top covered by a smooth layer of warm-cream icing. The icing stops at the upper edge rather than covering the sides, and the cake has no decorations or cut portions.

asset_specs.name: wicker basket
asset_specs.height: A child-sized carrying basket, about 35 cm long and 25 cm wide, carried in one hand by its handle.
asset_specs.spec: An oval basket woven from honey-brown willow wicker, with a flat base, gently flared sides, and a thick braided rim. A single rigid arched handle rises above the open top; there is no lid or fabric lining. At the start it contains one golden-brown oval loaf with three diagonal scores and one small round cake with cream icing, both visible inside.

asset_specs.name: Grandmother
asset_specs.height: An elderly woman slightly shorter than an average grown person, with a mild stoop.
asset_specs.spec: A slender elderly woman with warm light skin, a narrow, gently wrinkled face, brown eyes, and small round spectacles with thin dark-brown frames. Her silver-white hair is drawn into a small low bun. She wears a loose, ankle-length warm-cream nightdress with long sleeves and a high gathered neckline, a sage-green knitted shawl, and soft brown slippers.

asset_specs.name: wolf
asset_specs.height: A large natural wolf, reaching a grown person's waist at the shoulder when on all fours.
asset_specs.spec: A natural, unclothed wolf with a lean, long-legged body, a deep chest, large paws, and a long bushy tail; he normally moves on all fours rather than standing like a person. His fur is warm gray, with charcoal along his back and tail tip and pale cream on his muzzle, throat, and underside. He has a long tapered muzzle, a broad black nose, tall triangular ears, amber eyes, and prominent pointed white teeth.

asset_specs.name: daisies
asset_specs.height: Small plants about 15–25 cm tall, reaching an adult's ankle or lower shin.
asset_specs.spec: Small natural daisies growing in loose clumps, with slender green stems and narrow green leaves near their bases. Each flower has one round golden-yellow center surrounded by a single ring of slim white petals.

asset_specs.name: Grandmother’s nightcap
asset_specs.height: An adult-sized soft cap, small enough to cup in two hands.
asset_specs.spec: A white cotton nightcap with a softly rounded, roomy crown and a gathered opening edged by a narrow ruffle. Two narrow white ties extend from the lower edges, and the fabric has no pattern or colored trim.

asset_specs.name: Grandmother’s quilt
asset_specs.height: A single-bed-sized quilt, about 140 cm wide and 190 cm long.
asset_specs.spec: A thick rectangular patchwork quilt made from equal-sized squares alternating warm cream, sage green, and muted moss green in a repeating sequence. Small diamond-shaped stitches cross each square, and a solid moss-green binding runs around all four edges.

asset_specs.name: woodcutter
asset_specs.height: A tall grown man, about a head taller than Mother.
asset_specs.spec: A broad-shouldered, sturdy man with lightly tanned skin, brown eyes, short dark-brown hair, and a neatly trimmed brown beard. He wears a moss-green shirt with sleeves rolled to his elbows, dark-brown trousers, heavy brown leather boots, and a wide brown leather belt. A large pair of shears is secured in a leather loop on his belt, with its two black iron handles clearly exposed.

asset_specs.name: pair of shears
asset_specs.height: About 25 cm long, held and operated with one adult hand.
asset_specs.spec: A sturdy pair of shears with two straight, pointed silver-gray steel blades joined by a single round brass pivot. The handles are black iron loops, with one loop slightly larger than the other.

asset_specs.name: stones
asset_specs.height: Eight stones, each about 6–10 cm across and small enough to hold in one adult hand.
asset_specs.spec: Eight solid, irregularly oval stones with rounded edges and slightly uneven surfaces. They vary between medium gray and warm gray, with a few small tan flecks and no sharp points or markings.

asset_specs.name: needle
asset_specs.height: About 5 cm long, easily held between two fingertips.
asset_specs.spec: A straight, slender silver-colored steel sewing needle with a sharp point at one end. Its opposite end has a narrow oval eye, with no decorative details or attached handle.

asset_specs.height: A small spool about 4 cm high, fitting comfortably in one adult hand.
asset_specs.spec: Fine warm-ivory sewing thread wound neatly around a small natural-tan wooden spool. The spool has a narrow cylindrical center and two flat round ends, with a short loose end of thread resting against the winding.

plan.title: Little Red Riding Hood
plan.style: Watercolor and colored-pencil storybook illustrations; woodland greens, warm cream, and a scarlet cloak; soft morning sunlight outdoors, cool shadows inside the cottage, and warm light after the rescue.
plan.story:
Little Red Riding Hood’s mother tucked bread and a small cake into a wicker basket. “Take these to Grandmother’s cottage, where she keeps her quilt and nightcap on her bed and a needle and thread in her bedside sewing basket, and stay on the forest path, where daisies grow along the edges.” Red tied her scarlet hood and set off.

Under an oak tree, a wolf stepped onto the path. “Where are you going?” he asked.

“To Grandmother’s cottage beside the three birch trees,” Red replied.

“Why not bring her flowers?” suggested the wolf. While Red picked daisies, he raced ahead.

At the cottage’s green front door, the wolf knocked and called in a sweet voice, “It’s Little Red Riding Hood!”

“Lift the latch,” Grandmother answered from bed.

The wolf rushed inside and swallowed her whole. He put on her nightcap, pulled her quilt over himself, and waited.

Red arrived, pushed open the green door, and placed her basket on the wooden table. She approached the bed.

“Grandmother, what big ears you have!”

“All the better to hear you with.”

“What big eyes you have!”

“All the better to see you with.”

Red gripped her cloak. “What big teeth you have!”

“All the better to eat you with!”

The wolf sprang up. Red screamed, but he swallowed her whole. Then he fell asleep, snoring loudly.

A passing woodcutter heard the snores and entered through the green door. Seeing the wolf’s swollen belly, he took a pair of shears from his belt and carefully snipped it open. Red scrambled out, then helped Grandmother climb free. Trembling with relief, they hugged.

They filled the sleeping wolf’s belly with stones gathered from outside the cottage. Grandmother stitched the wolf’s belly shut with a needle and thread from her bedside sewing basket. When he awoke, he stumbled and fell dead.

Grandmother shared the cake with her rescuers. Red promised never to wander from the path again.

beats.text: Grandmother’s cottage stands beside three birch trees.
The wolf runs toward the cottage’s green front door, away from us.
He knocks on the door.
He calls through the door in a sweet voice.
It’s Little Red Riding Hood!

story_lines: At the cottage’s green front door, the wolf knocked and called in a sweet voice, “It’s Little Red Riding Hood!”

beats.text: Grandmother lies beneath a quilt in the bed on the right.
A nightcap rests beside her pillow.
A sewing basket stands beside the bed.
Lift the latch.
The latch rises on the green door at the back of the room.
The door swings inward.
The wolf rushes through the doorway toward the bed on the right.
He opens his jaws wide over Grandmother.
Grandmother disappears whole into his mouth.
The wolf swallows.
He climbs onto the bed.
He picks up the nightcap from beside the pillow.
He pulls the nightcap onto his head.
He draws the quilt over himself.
The wolf lies still with his eyes on the green door.

story_lines: “Lift the latch,” Grandmother answered from bed.
The wolf rushed inside and swallowed her whole.
He put on her nightcap, pulled her quilt over himself, and waited.

beats.text: The green door swings inward beneath Little Red Riding Hood’s hand.
Little Red Riding Hood enters toward us, carrying her wicker basket.
She places the basket on the wooden table to the left.
She crosses right toward the bed.
The wolf’s large ears stick out from under the nightcap.
Grandmother, what big ears you have!
All the better to hear you with.
The wolf’s large eyes follow her.
What big eyes you have!
All the better to see you with.
Little Red Riding Hood grips her cloak.
What big teeth you have!
All the better to eat you with!
The wolf springs up from beneath the quilt.
Little Red Riding Hood screams.
The wolf opens his jaws over her.
Little Red Riding Hood disappears whole into his mouth.
The wolf swallows.
He slumps back onto the bed.
His eyes close.
Loud snores rumble from his open mouth.

story_lines: Red arrived, pushed open the green door, and placed her basket on the wooden table.
She approached the bed.
“Grandmother, what big ears you have!”
“All the better to hear you with.”
“What big eyes you have!”
“All the better to see you with.”
Red gripped her cloak.
“What big teeth you have!”
“All the better to eat you with!”
The wolf sprang up.
Red screamed, but he swallowed her whole.
Then he fell asleep, snoring loudly.

beats.text: A woodcutter walks from left to right past the cottage, shears hanging from his belt.
The wolf’s snores carry through the green doorway.
The woodcutter stops.
He turns toward the green door.
He steps through the doorway, away from us.

story_lines: A passing woodcutter heard the snores and entered through the green door.

beats.text: The woodcutter approaches the bed on the right.
His gaze settles on the wolf’s swollen belly.
He draws the quilt down from the belly.
He takes the shears from his belt.
He makes small, careful snips along the wolf’s belly.
The cut parts into an opening.
Little Red Riding Hood scrambles through the opening onto the quilt.
She reaches back into the opening.
Grandmother takes her hands.
Little Red Riding Hood pulls as Grandmother climbs free onto the bed.
Little Red Riding Hood and Grandmother tremble.
They hug.
The woodcutter returns the shears to his belt.

story_lines: Seeing the wolf’s swollen belly, he took a pair of shears from his belt and carefully snipped it open.
Red scrambled out, then helped Grandmother climb free.
Trembling with relief, they hugged.

beats.text: The woodcutter gathers stones from the ground into his arms.
Little Red Riding Hood gathers stones in the lifted hem of her cloak.
Grandmother gathers stones against her chest.
They carry the stones toward the green front door on the right.

story_lines: They filled the sleeping wolf’s belly with stones gathered from outside the cottage.

beats.text: The woodcutter carries his stones through the green door toward the bed.
Little Red Riding Hood follows with stones cradled in her cloak.
Grandmother follows with stones in her arms.
The wolf snores with his eyes closed.
The woodcutter lowers his stones through the opening in the wolf’s belly.
Little Red Riding Hood tips her stones into the opening.
Grandmother adds her stones to the belly.
Grandmother lifts a needle and thread from her bedside sewing basket.
She passes the thread through the needle’s eye.
She stitches the wolf’s belly shut.

story_lines: They filled the sleeping wolf’s belly with stones gathered from outside the cottage.
Grandmother stitched the wolf’s belly shut with a needle and thread from her bedside sewing basket.

beats.text: The wolf’s eyes open.
He climbs out of the bed toward us.
He stumbles forward under the weight of his belly.
He falls heavily onto the floor.
The wolf lies motionless, his eyes fixed and his chest still.

story_lines: When he awoke, he stumbled and fell dead.

beats.text: Grandmother, Little Red Riding Hood and the woodcutter sit around the wooden table.
Grandmother lifts the small cake from the wicker basket.
She breaks the cake into three pieces.
She gives one piece to Little Red Riding Hood on her left.
She gives another piece to the woodcutter on her right.
She takes the remaining piece.
I promise never to wander from the path again.

story_lines: Grandmother shared the cake with her rescuers.
Red promised never to wander from the path again.
